clue.text: Inferior newspaper that's a bit old fashioned

parts.note: to be behind is to lag, to be lower in rank or standard
The Times is a long-running British national daily paper

explanation.surface: A down-market tabloid is accused of being rather dated.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TIMES is a British national daily newspaper, so the clue reads as someone sneering at a rival paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To be out of date is to lag behind current fashion, an idiom for being old-fashioned.

clue.text: Relative accommodated in hotel journalist regularly visited

indicators.note: something accommodated in a place is housed inside it, so the relative sits within the other letters

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ED is short for editor, the usual crossword journalist
an aunt is a family relative

explanation.surface: A family member put up at a hotel is visited often by a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A place frequented again and again by someone, especially a ghost, is said to be haunted by them.

clue.text: North American English has a reputation

explanation.surface: Someone from North America who is English has a certain standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A good name is a good standing, so the word is a synonym for one's public reputation.

clue.text: Run back to university, looking embarrassed to be punished

indicators.note: back tells the solver to read the word for run from right to left

parts.note: to trot is to run at a gentle pace
someone embarrassed goes red in the face

explanation.surface: A student is sent running back to college, red-faced, to face punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a student sent back to college red-faced; 'back' turns the trotting word round to give TORT, the legal wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tortured has been made to suffer pain deliberately, a harsh form of being punished.

clue.text: Cut out physical exertion, without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the hesitation sound is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: exercise is physical exertion
ER is the sound of hesitating in speech

explanation.surface: Advice to give up working out, and to do so decisively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes ER from EXERCISE, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise something is to remove it surgically, a formal synonym for cutting it out.

clue.text: Storm into the final, getting furious

indicators.note: into places the word for storm inside the word for the final

parts.note: the end is the final part
to rage is to storm angrily

explanation.surface: A team storms through to the final, its supporters wild with excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a team storming into a final; here 'Storm' is a verb meaning to rage, and 'into' places it inside the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To be made extremely angry is to be incensed, a synonym for furious.

clue.text: Spirit is on the menu for selected candidates

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: describing candidates chosen for a final list

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits such as whisky
a dish on the menu is listed there

explanation.surface: A pub's spirits appear on the menu for the people chosen to compete.
explanation.walkthrough: A SHORT is British pub talk for a small glass of spirits such as whisky or gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates picked from a larger field for final consideration are put on a short list.

clue.text: In France you get marine rice dish with seasoning

parts.note: tu is French for you
RM stands for Royal Marine

indicators.note: dish as a verb means to ruin, so the letters of rice are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Dining in France, you are served a seafood rice dish with spices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' looks like part of a menu, a seafood rice dish, but is a verb meaning to spoil, turning the rice letters into ERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow ground root is a spice, used to season and colour curries.

clue.text: A rash sort of girl?

indicators.note: sort as a verb means to arrange, so these letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A question about whether a girl is the impetuous type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' reorders the letters of A RASH.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common female first name, so the girl is an example.

clue.text: Organise urgent aid — it could be met with this!

definitions.text: Organise urgent aid — it could be met with this!

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange, so the letters of these words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A cynical warning that charitable relief may not be thanked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organise' rearranges URGENT AID IT; the whole clue then wryly describes the reception aid may get.
explanation.definitionFit: Failure to give thanks for help received is the very lack of gratitude that relief may meet.

clue.text: Heads get shock read back

indicators.note: read back tells the solver to take the word for shock from right to left

parts.note: to stun is to shock

explanation.surface: Leaders receive a shock when something is read out again.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut is slang for the head, so heads are nuts in the plural.

clue.text: Western man makes weapons stay behind

parts.note: guns are weapons
to linger is to stay behind after others leave

explanation.surface: A cowboy picks up his guns and hangs around after the others go.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun-toting fighter is a stock figure of the cowboy film, a man from the Western.

clue.text: They may fix broken toes with old ways

indicators.note: broken means the letters of toes are smashed into a new order

parts.note: paths are ways

explanation.surface: Practitioners might mend broken toes by traditional methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges TOES to OSTE, followed by O and PATHS.
explanation.definitionFit: These practitioners treat bones and joints by manipulation, so they mend skeletal problems.

clue.text: Vegetables god serves?

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
to dish up is to serve, so dishes means serves

explanation.surface: A question whether a deity hands out greens.
explanation.definitionFit: These red-skinned roots are salad vegetables.

clue.text: Vehicle American attorney left to a hooligan

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
a DA is a District Attorney in the US

explanation.surface: An American lawyer leaves a van to a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wilfully damages property is a thug or hooligan.

clue.text: Depressed before strike, but not stressed

indicators.note: before places the word for depressed ahead of the word for strike

parts.note: down means depressed or low
to beat is to strike

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy ahead of an industrial strike, though not anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed' looks like the definition, and the answer can mean that, but here it gives DOWN; the definition is the relaxed, low-key sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Downbeat can mean relaxed and understated, the opposite of tense.

clue.text: How to lay it on thick, and let row develop?

definitions.text: How to lay it on thick

indicators.note: to develop is to change form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice on how to exaggerate, and to let an argument grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develop' rearranges LET ROW. To lay it on with a trowel is an idiom for flattering grossly.
explanation.definitionFit: The bricklayer's flat-bladed tool spreads mortar thickly, giving the idiom laying it on with one.

clue.text: Player discovered in turbo-car in accident

indicators.note: discovered in means the answer is found inside the run of these words

explanation.surface: A musician is found inside a turbo car after a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: This small egg-shaped wind instrument is played, so it is a player of music in crossword sense.

clue.text: Food for which forage is unfortunately necessary

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A delicacy that sadly requires foraging to produce.
explanation.definitionFit: This rich liver pâté from fattened geese or ducks is a luxury dish.

clue.text: Plant covering cold lake before the end of June

clue.text: Hobo with no pedigree becomes a bouncer

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp
O is zero or nothing, so no
a line is a family line of descent, a pedigree

explanation.definitionFit: A sprung mat on which people jump repeatedly is something that bounces, hence a bouncer.

clue.text: Puffed, say, and downhearted

parts.note: blew means puffed out breath

explanation.surface: Someone who is out of breath and feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sad is being in low spirits, a colloquial colour for being downhearted.

clue.text: Line up for a storyteller

explanation.surface: Instructions to queue for a narrator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RAIL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tells untruths is a fibber, and telling stories is a euphemism for lying.

clue.text: Import from Germany before split

indicators.note: before puts the letter for Germany ahead of the word for split

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a rift is a split

explanation.surface: Goods are brought in from Germany ahead of a falling-out.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of a speech is its general meaning or gist, the same as its import.

clue.text: Believed to have made a financial deposit

explanation.surface: Someone is trusted because they paid money into the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a story is to believe it, and to credit an account is to pay money into it.

clue.text: Tribesman fends off dog

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: The well-known phrase for a canine companion, loyal to people.
